claims.summary: Hole-cost restriction (binary: 0/1-valued definitions): over every field, in the multilinear ring, let PHP^{m,r}_n be Razborov's all-subsets system (imp:razborov-generic-pigeonhole-degree) with C(m,r)>n, and add M nonrecursive extension axioms z_i-Q_i, Q_i multilinear 0/1-valued (Q_i^2=Q_i; automatic over F_2) in the x's of degree <=k, k>=1. (a) Every refutation has degree >=(n/2+1)/k, by the ring map z_i -> Q_i. (b) If n>=4, every monomial of every Q_i has fewer than r variables on any one hole (implied by k<r) and each Q_i touches at most eta<=n/4 holes, every PC refutation of size s (total monomials) has ln s >= n^2/(64k(mn+M eta)) - 1, by restrictions averaging separately over holes (one hole per step) and over extension variables (a zero of Q_i, then its <=eta holes removed), then (a). (b) is a restriction variant of the plain route (a) plus a size-degree tradeoff, the binary analogue of Dahiya-Mahajan-Mouli's Theorem 5.5 (stated for p>2); vacuous once M eta >= n^2/(64k).
claims.assessment: Working proof, method not new: (a) is the degree step of the route ctx:pc-extension-variables-literature records; (b) is stronger than that route (reviewer's unverified computation with an unread tradeoff) exactly when 64c(mn+M eta) < k(mn+M). Passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with corrections.
